chunks: Al-Bazawfari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who wrote to his wife regarding her divorce and wrote regarding the freeing of his slave, but his tongue did not speak it. He said, 'It is not valid until his tongue speaks it.'
ai.seo_question: Is a written divorce or manumission valid without verbal pronunciation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition of verbal articulation (*nutf*) for the validity of divorce (*talaq*) and manumission (*itq*), distinguishing between mere written intent and effective legal declaration. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the spoken word as the operative mechanism for these acts, ensuring clarity and preventing ambiguity in personal status law. The hadith highlights that while writing serves as evidence, it does not substitute for the physical act of pronouncing the formula, a principle derived from the Prophetic tradition of verbalizing legal acts.
